provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. Colour roles are fixed as constants: FOUR = palette[4] and SIX = palette[6]. It finds the motif as the bounding box of the FOUR cells. Noise never uses colour 4, so the only FOUR cells are the motif's, and its 4s span all three rows and columns. It then lists the motif's distinct orientations (up to 8: rotations and mirrors) and tries every placement, including placements partly off the grid. A placement is a match when every SIX of the oriented motif lands on an in-grid SIX cell and no in-grid FOUR-position holds SIX or FOUR. The motif itself, in its own orientation at its own box, is skipped. Each match gets FOUR painted on its in-grid FOUR-positions. This is the same match test the constructor's _scan uses and the archived solver applies. The orientation search covers the whole dihedral group, and the motif is read from the visible grid. So any D4 transform of the episode just turns visible copies into other members of the visible motif's orbit. No direction or axis constant is needed, and d4 is intentionally unused. Blocked near-copies are rejected because one of their FOUR-positions holds SIX. Clipped copies are accepted because off-grid FOUR-positions are ignored.
draft_notes.limitations: d4 is not used, because the mechanism is invariant under the dihedral group. The program assumes that palette[4] appears only in the motif, as the constructor guarantees. If the query has no palette[4] cell, the grid is returned unchanged. The constructor's repair step is a bounded loop that removes accidental matches. If the repair fails, generate() retries the whole scene, so accepted scenes have exactly the intended matches. Removing blocked near-copies is only best effort, but they never satisfy the match test, so this cannot change the answer. Demonstrations are not consulted. Neither the fixtures nor the constructor contradict the uniform rule, and I found no constructor defects that affect the visible mechanism. I have not run any tests.
